# Introduction {#sec-introduction}

This document is an example. It is the reference for how a guideline is written
so that the publishing pipeline renders it in the AARC design. The text of each
section states the convention that the section shows.

## Notational Conventions {#sec-notational-conventions}

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT,
RECOMMENDED, NOT RECOMMENDED, MAY and OPTIONAL in this document are to be
interpreted as described in BCP 14 [@RFC2119; @RFC8174] when, and only when,
they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

## Terminology {#sec-terminology}

This section is normative. A term is written as a definition list:

Trust Authority : A third party which is trusted to identify entities
[@OID-Fed].

SP-IdP-Proxy : The component of an AAI that acts as a Service Provider towards
the Identity Providers and as an Identity Provider towards the services, as
defined by the AARC Blueprint Architecture [@AARC-G045].

## Scope of this document {#sec-scope}

The headings carry no numbers in the source. The pipeline numbers them, and a
reference to a section is written as `@sec-scope`, which renders as @sec-scope.

# Trust Model {#sec-trust-model}

@fig-trust-model shows two proxies that trust a common Trust Authority. A figure
is an image file in the `figures/` directory of the guideline. SVG keeps the
text sharp at any size.

![Simple federation model based on the use of a common Trust
Authority.](figures/trust-model.svg){#fig-trust-model
width="75%"}

A requirement is written in the body text and states its profile in brackets,
for example:

- [G100.1] A Proxy MUST publish an Entity Configuration.
- [G100.2] A Proxy SHOULD validate the Trust Marks of its peers.

@tbl-registration compares the two methods of client registration. A table whose
cells hold only a line of text is a pipe table, as @tbl-registration is.

| Aspect       | Automatic registration          | Explicit registration                 |
| ------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Mechanism    | No prior registration           | The RP registers before the first use |
| Client ID    | The federation entity ID of RP  | Assigned by the OP                    |
| Requirements | The OP MUST resolve trust chain | The OP MUST resolve trust chain       |

: Client registration methods {#tbl-registration}

A table whose cells hold a list or several paragraphs is a list table, as
@tbl-trade-offs is. Each item of the list is a row, each item of a row is a
cell, and the first row is the header. The paragraph before the list is the
caption. A grid table holds the same content, but prettier flattens it, so a
guideline does not use one.

::: {.list-table #tbl-trade-offs tbl-colwidths="[20,40,40]"}

Trade-offs of the registration methods

- - Aspect
  - Automatic registration
  - Explicit registration
- - Pros
  - - No need for prior contact
    - Fully dynamic
  - - More control
    - Allows policy checks before registration
- - Cons
  - - Policies are evaluated at runtime
  - - Requires client-side registration logic
    - The registration expires and has to be renewed

:::

Every `:::` line stands alone, with a blank line before and after it. Without
them, prettier joins the line to the text beside it, and the block is lost.

::: {.callout-note title="Note"}

A callout sets a passage apart from the normative text. It is not normative.

:::

# Entity Configuration {#sec-entity-configuration}

Code is written as a fenced block. The language name is optional.

```json
{
  "iss": "https://proxy.example.org",
  "sub": "https://proxy.example.org",
  "authority_hints": ["https://ta.example.org"],
  "metadata": {
    "openid_provider": {
      "issuer": "https://proxy.example.org"
    }
  }
}
```

Inline code, such as `authority_hints`, is set in the same font.

# Summary of Required Features {#sec-summary}

A wide table is placed on a landscape page with a `landscape` div. The heading
goes inside the div, so that it stands on the same page as the table.

| Role            | Entity Configuration                | Client Registration       | Trust Marks                | Metadata Policies    | Endpoints               |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Trust Authority | MUST publish `federation_entity`    | N/A                       | [G100.2] MUST list issuers | [G100.2] MAY enforce | [REQ] Fetch, [OPT] List |
| Proxy (OP role) | MUST publish `openid_provider`      | MUST support both methods | [G100.2] MUST validate     | [G100.2] MUST apply  | [REQ] Registration      |
| Proxy (RP role) | MUST publish `openid_relying_party` | MUST implement one method | [G100.2] MUST validate     | [G100.2] MUST apply  |                         |

: Features by participant role {#tbl-summary}

:::
